why: Replacing the four examples with measured Japanese cases that penalize isolating sentence-final predicates/auxiliaries moved the model away from placing cuts immediately before clause-final material, yielding most of the measured gain in the mid-to-long latency bins (≤7–≤10). However the model overcorrected in many instances by shifting cuts into internal morpheme/character boundaries (fragmenting words and particles), producing the large negative tail moves despite the net positive bin-level effect.
lesson: Keep the emphasis that cutting off clause‑final predicates/auxiliaries is harmful, but avoid example edits that encourage overcorrection into internal-word/particle fragmentation.
